definition: Scoring the reasoning rather than the answer, and across 7 sources the evaluation the archive keeps finding is necessary and rarely done. Its measured motivation: high answer accuracy conceals near-total failure at producing or reasoning from required visual aids; a benchmark of mathematical proof reveals failure modes an answer check cannot see; and error-detection benchmarks show frontier models about 10 points behind human evaluation at saying where a chain went wrong. Two construction approaches appear -- symbolic generation so that every intermediate quantity is verifiable by construction, and expert annotation of the specific span that establishes a conclusion, which one source uses to show that predicting the right answer and giving the right reason are separable abilities. The archive's standing caution is that a step score computed by a model inherits that model's reliability, and that agreement with one reference derivation penalises a different valid one.

evidence.note: Benchmarks whether multimodal models can construct visual aids for geometry problems, and finds high answer accuracy conceals near-total failure at producing or reasoning from those aids.
evidence.title: VisAidMath: Benchmarking Visual-Aided Mathematical Reasoning

evidence.note: Uses 200 mathematical proof problems as a diagnostic, finding some reasoning models solve under 20% and cataloguing 10 fine-grained error types that numerical benchmarks hide.
evidence.title: Mathematical Proof as a Litmus Test: Revealing Failure Modes of Advanced Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: A financial reasoning benchmark built from parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python, giving machine-verifiable step-level ground truth and contamination-free regeneration.
evidence.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning

evidence.note: Benchmarks multimodal models on detecting and categorizing errors in K-12 math solutions collected from real student interactions, with the best model about 10% behind human experts.
evidence.title: ErrorRadar: Benchmarking Complex Mathematical Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models Via Error Detection

evidence.note: Shows evaluator accuracy improves monotonically with reasoning tokens spent, and that buying compute at evaluation time can substitute for buying it at generation time.
evidence.title: Scaling Evaluation-Time Compute with Reasoning Models as Evaluators

evidence.note: A multimodal scientific reasoning benchmark over 54 subfields with domain-specific visuals and expert solutions for 46% of items, scoring the reasoning process as well as the answer.
evidence.title: SciVQR: A Multidisciplinary Multimodal Benchmark for Advanced Scientific Reasoning Evaluation

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: process evaluation
